editorial:
Imagine living with a landlord who is so cheap he would charge you for the air you breathe. That is exactly what you get with Rigsby, a grumpy man who scams his two lodgers, John and Philip, by making them pay full price for a single shared room. The vibe here is pure old-school British chaos. You will love watching Rigsby try to act like a big shot while everyone around him sees right through his lies. The best part is the romantic tension, as Rigsby tries to flirt with Miss Jones, but she is way more interested in Philip. It is a funny, awkward mess that feels like a stage play brought to life.

What really makes this work is the acting, especially the way the characters bounce off each other with fast, witty dialogue. The pacing is snappy, and while it is a simple story, the comedy comes from how pathetic Rigsby is. If you like sitcoms where the bad guy always loses, you will have a blast. Since it is an older film, you might want to track down the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture quality, or just look for a digital rental on Apple TV for a quick laugh with friends.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with Rigsby getting exactly what he deserves. After spending the whole time trying to cheat his tenants and chase Miss Jones, his lies finally catch up to him. He ends up totally defeated and alone, while Philip and John get the last laugh. There is no big happy ending for the landlord; instead, he is left in his own misery, proving that being a greedy jerk never pays off in the end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic British humor and seeing greedy people fail.
similarMovies: Monty Python and the Holy Grail
